full_judgment: 6. It is alleged that the subsequent suit was barred by limitation under Article 113 of the Limitation Act as the cause of action arose on 16.5.1976 as disclosed in paragraphs 13 and 6 of the plaint to Title Suit No. 263 of 1976 and the Title Suit No. 874 of 1979 respectively. It was further stated that as in the subsequent suit Schedule-'A' property of the petitioner was mortgaged with the House Building Finance Corporation in a Loan Case No. HB-D-5376 of 1970 the suit suffers from defect of parties as the Corporation was not impleaded in the suit which contested the earlier suit by filing written statement. It is further alleged that the suit was instituted on 7.12.1979 and the court fixed on 20.12.1979 for service return unusually within a short period and within 3 days a fraudulent appearance of the defendant 1 was recorded on 11.12.1979 on the filing of a fictitious vakalatnama followed by an application praying for time to file written statement although the date for appearance on 20.12.1979 was fixed. On that date the plain tiff got another application filed in the' name of petitioner praying for time for 7 days to file written statement and both the application and the power are forged and fraudulent. It was further alleged that the order No. 2 to order No, 6 were not written by an official of the Court but the plaintiff got the same written in collusion which some outsiders which is against the provisions of Article 874 of the CRO(Vol-1). It is further alleged that all service returns from Civil Revision No. 1042 of 1978 down to Title Execution Case No. 24 of 1980 will show that on all occasions the plaintiff procured the services of the same process server, Fariduddin, who particularly submitted on 8.12.1979 service return of the later suit which was contrary to Order 5 rule 18 CPC and Article 70(1) of the CRO (Vol-1) as no name of any person witnessing service of summons was noted in the service return. The trial Court on 15.2.1980 passed the ex parte decree on the basis of such service or summons. It is further alleged that after obtaining the ex parte decree the opposite party 1 with evil design moved this Division on IS.4.1980 to discharge the Rule without disclosing about anything regarding institution of Title Suit No. 874 of 1979 and obtained an order of discharge on 15.,4.1980, After the discharge of the aforesaid Rule on 15.4.1980 heput the said illegal decree in execution on 2.5.1980 in Title execution Case No. 24 of 1980 behind the back of the petitioner suppressing the process and gaining over the said process server Fariduddin and ultimately got the deed of exchange registered through court without getting permission from the House Building Finance Corporation. It is further alleged that the registration of the document was null and void according to Article 21 (5) of the Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation Order, 1973 and after obtaining this void document the plaintiff got the writ of khas possession although in the application under Order 21 rule 11 (2) CPC he did not pray so. The petitioner in execution of the said writ was evicted from the property on 3.10.80 during the vacation of the civil Court on which date she came to know about the institution of this suit. Till 1.11.1980 the civil Court was on vacation and on that date she applied for certified copies of ex parte judgment and decree dated 15.2.1980 and 17.3.1980 respectively which were made ready on 20.1.1981 and was obtained on 16.2.1981 and on that very date the petitioner filed the Title Appeal No. 32 of 1981. The memorandum of the appeal was accompanied by an application under section S of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay in filing the appeal stating that the appellant was kept out of knowledge about the ex-pane decree due to fraud practised by the opposite party 1. The appeal was registered on 16.2.1981 and the application for condonation of delay was taken up for hearing on 18.2.1981 but the learned District Judge ordered to decide the condonation application at the time of hearing of the appeal and called for a report from the civil Court as to whether the orders of the Title Suit No. 874 of 1979 from order Nos. 2 to 6 were written by the outsider as alleged and the learned court was informed on 11.3.1981 about the same that the order-sheet was written by the outsiders. .
